answer: After simplification, LINE measures the distance between the conditional distributions p2(·|v_i) (the model) and p̂2(·|v_i) = w_ij/d_i (the empirical network distribution) with the Kullback-Leibler divergence. Dropping constant terms (the degree-based weights λ_i = d_i and the fixed normalization) gives O2 = -Σ_{(i,j)∈E} w_ij · log p2(v_j|v_i), where p2(v_j|v_i) = exp(u_j^T u_i) / Σ_{k∈V} exp(u_k^T u_i), with u_i the vertex embedding and u_j the context embedding of vertex j.
confidence_reasoning: I recall the LINE paper's use of KL divergence and the resulting log-likelihood form of O2 with moderate confidence, but exact notation and which constant terms are dropped may differ from the paper.
